thread:
maria.g: Quick heads-up — ACME onboarding scheduled Wed EOD. They want private deployment (VPC) with customer-managed egress and strict IP allowlist. Need to lock acceptance gates and call out edge cases before we sign-off.
aj: Got it. Do we have their network diagram? who owns routing?
maria.g: They sent a simple diagram: prod VPC -> transit -> our peering. They emphasised no customer-facing NATs on our side; customer will manage egress NAT.
chen: Important: we need a clear plan for healthchecks and control-plane reachability if customer blocks outbound traffic. That's a common fail.
sophie: +1. Also need to clarify DNS expectations. Are they providing DNS for model pulls & updates or is that on our side?
maria.g: They want to resolve our private service hostnames via their DNS forwarders. We asked for a fallback: our side must support explicit host entries if customer DNS flaps.
raul: Edge-case: what if customer's firewall strips TLS SNI? Our certs require SNI for hostname routing when multiple tenants share IPs. We should request NAT or dedicated IPs.
aj: Can we enumerate acceptance criteria now? I'll draft and we can hand to solutions team.
chen: Draft checklist — minimal (short bullets):
```
- Control plane reachability verified from customer network (ports 443, 5222 for agent)
- Verified egress handoff: customer NAT IPs provided and stable for 7 days
- DNS resolution test: forwards + fallback hosts added to /etc/hosts on agent nodes
- Cert/SNI validation pass for all endpoints
- KV/cache sync test under packet loss
- Rollback plan tested (ability to disable peering and switch to hosted fallback)
```
sophie: Add: agreed SLAs for control-plane reconnection time (max 2 mins) and an incident escalation contact list.
maria.g: Good. Also confirm logging & audit: customer wants all inference logs to stay in their VPC and only our metrics to be exported to Redwood. Need KMS handoff notes.
raul: For logs, we need to confirm: do we push logs to a customer S3/GCS endpoint via presigned URLs, or do they run a log collector in their VPC? That affects egress requirements.
aj: For presigned S3 approach we need stable egress + time-synced machine. For collector approach we need open 9000/5000 etc. Which does ACME prefer?
maria.g: They prefer a collector inside their VPC. So they'll open inbound to collector; we push via peering.
chen: Action item: define network handoff matrix (who provides IPs, DNS, certs, collectors, ports). I'll put a table in the PRD.
raul: Risk: customer-managed egress means we cannot source-validate X-Forwarded-For headers reliably. Flagging for product: authentication flows relying on client IP may break.
sophie: Noted. Product needs to own fallback auth token path for these deployments.
aj: Also need list of test cases for acceptance:
- BGP flapping simulation
- DNS forwarder latency (500ms bursts)
- Partial packet loss 1-2%
- Collector restart and log reingestion
- Circuit switch to hosted fallback (< 60s)

maria.g: Can someone volunteer to run an initial tabletop with the ACME SREs Thurs? I can host.
chen: I can join and run the BGP and DNS tests.
raul: I'll prepare the TLS/SNI and cert rotation notes.
sophie: I'll prepare the SLA & escalation doc and the KMS integration checklist.
deploy-bot: Reminder: private-deploy-onprem-template v2 was updated 3 days ago — verify local changes against template. Link: https://redwood.internal/templates/private-deploy-v2
maria.g: Thanks. After the tabletop we'll update the PRD and post the final acceptance criteria here. Can we aim to freeze gates by Friday EOD?
aj: Yes — I'll update the draft and ping solutions for legal/network verbiage.
chen: FYI: request to product — include explicit support matrix for "customer-managed-egress" in our hub so support knows when to escalate to eng-platform.
sophie: I'll open a quick work item in the roadmap tracker and tag eng-platform + support.
maria.g: Great. Closing loop: action owners — aj (PRD draft), chen (network handoff table + tests), raul (TLS/certs), sophie (SLA/KMS & escalation). We'll sync again after tabletop. :thumbsup:
